tools.name: get_person_profile
tools.description: Look up one person by exactly one identifier: `profile` (LinkedIn profile URL or username), `email`, `twitter`, `facebook` or `github`. Optional sections add data to the answer and to the cost of the call: `socialLink`, `phoneNumber`, `personalEmail`, `workEmail`, `careerInsight`, `developerProfile`, `activities`. Ask only for the sections you need: a full profile may not fit the client's limit on tool output (25,000 tokens in Claude Code). `personalEmail` and `workEmail` return only addresses validated as deliverable. To find someone's work email from a profile URL, pass `profile` and `workEmail: "include"`: an empty `contactInformation.emails.work` means no work email was found here, and find_work_emails with the person's name and company domain may still find candidates. `maxAgeSeconds` is the oldest cached copy you accept (default 30 days, usually answered in seconds). A small value starts a live lookup, which is slower and costs more: it can take up to 5 minutes and run past the time limit of the MCP client. A call cut off before the answer arrives may still be charged. To get the copy that was saved in the meantime, call again without maxAgeSeconds; do not repeat a live lookup right away. The result has the full v3 answer in `data`, the credits charged for the call in `creditCost` and the `requestId` to quote to support.

socialLink.description: Include the social profile URLs, returned in the `contactInformation.socialLinks` section, along with the corresponding usernames in the `slug` section. Default: exclude.

phoneNumber.description: Include phone numbers, returned in the `contactInformation.phoneNumbers` section. Default: exclude.

personalEmail.description: Include personal emails, returned in the `contactInformation.emails.personal` section. Default: exclude.

workEmail.description: Include work emails, returned in the `contactInformation.emails.work` section. Default: exclude.

careerInsight.description: Include the estimated salary, seniority, and inferred skills, returned in the `careerInsight` section. Default: exclude.

developerProfile.description: Include the GitHub developer profile data, returned in the `developerProfile` section. Default: exclude.

activities.description: Include up to 100 of the most recent posts from the person page, newest first with undated posts last, returned in the `activities` section. Default: exclude.

maxAgeSeconds.description: Maximum acceptable age of cached data, in seconds. Default: 2592000.

tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: Look up a company by its LinkedIn company or showcase page URL (`url`). Optional sections add data to the answer and to the cost of the call: `fundingData`, `exitData`, `acquisitions`, `extra`, `activities`. Ask only for the sections you need: a full profile may not fit the client's limit on tool output (25,000 tokens in Claude Code). `maxAgeSeconds` is the oldest cached copy you accept (default 30 days, usually answered in seconds). A small value starts a live lookup, which is slower and costs more: it can take up to 5 minutes and run past the time limit of the MCP client. A call cut off before the answer arrives may still be charged. To get the copy that was saved in the meantime, call again without maxAgeSeconds; do not repeat a live lookup right away. The result has the full v3 answer in `data`, the credits charged for the call in `creditCost` and the `requestId` to quote to support.

url.description: LinkedIn company or showcase page URL to look up.

fundingData.description: Include the funding rounds, returned in the `funding.rounds` section. Default: exclude.

exitData.description: Include the exit events, returned in the `exits` section. Default: exclude.

acquisitions.description: Include the companies acquired and the acquirer, returned in the `acquisitions` section. Default: exclude.

extra.description: Include the extra profile details: the Crunchbase URL, rounds count, total funding and investor count in the `funding.summary` section, the ticker symbol and IPO status in the `stock` section, and the contact email and Crunchbase link in the `contactInformation` section. Default: exclude.

activities.description: Include up to 100 of the most recent posts from the company page, newest first with undated posts last, returned in the `activities` section. Default: exclude.

maxAgeSeconds.description: Maximum acceptable age of cached data, in seconds. Default: 2592000.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Search companies by name (`q`). Returns up to 10 matches with the company name, logo URL, domain, industry, size, location and LinkedIn URL; pass the LinkedIn URL to get_company_profile for the full profile. The result has the full v3 answer in `data`, the credits charged for the call in `creditCost` and the `requestId` to quote to support.

tools.name: search_company_logos
tools.description: Find companies by name or domain (`q`) and get their logo URLs, with the company name, domain and LinkedIn URL. The result has the full v3 answer in `data`, the credits charged for the call in `creditCost` and the `requestId` to quote to support.

q.description: Company name or domain to search for.

tools.name: find_work_emails
tools.description: Find work email candidates for a person at a company: pass `full_name`, or `first_name` and/or `last_name`, together with the company `domain`. Each candidate has a validation verdict in `validity` — `valid`, `invalid`, `catchall`, `malformed` or another value; only `valid` is confirmed deliverable. `limit` caps the number of candidates (1–10). The result has the full v3 answer in `data`, the credits charged for the call in `creditCost` and the `requestId` to quote to support.

domain.description: Company domain to scope the lookup.

limit.description: Maximum number of email candidates to return.

tools.name: validate_email
tools.description: Check whether one email address is deliverable. `emailStatus` is the verdict — `valid`, `invalid`, `catchall`, `malformed` or another value; when the domain belongs to a known company, a company summary is attached. The result has the full v3 answer in `data`, the credits charged for the call in `creditCost` and the `requestId` to quote to support.
